title: I Used the Seed-Library Checkout on the Volunteer Who Pocketed My Packets

parts.text: I opened the seed drawer at 11:04 a.m. and volunteer Maren was already tucking our numbered packets into her tote. The card said: SIX PACKETS. SIGN THE LOG. RETURNS BY FROST. I was thirty-five, library steward, holding a catalog that listed our lot. Maren shrugged. "Volunteers are the drawer." I photographed the card, the log, and her tote on our counter. Then I asked for the checkout sheet. At 11:12 the desk pinged why Maren's name was on our six. I kept my voice library-soft and let the timestamp talk. A card is only a card until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The desk can see Maren's tote on our counter during our checkout.

social.video_title: She pocketed our numbered packets from the drawer — Part 1/2
social.description: Seed library, a volunteer on our counter, a six-packet log she posted. I logged the tote. Would you have asked for the checkout sheet?

parts.text: Maren called it a hold until the desk asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the card, and the tote still. The packets went back to our drawer. Maren ran her own six and told the next volunteer atmosphere was always about sharing. Sharing is a word volunteers use when a log exists. Drawer policy now has a second line: VOLUNTEERS ARE NOT THE DRAWER. I keep our lot on a labeled bin. Maren brown-bags her jokes. The library finally looks like a checkout, not a tote. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.
